newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - More basis bids rolled to July.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - More basis bids rolled to July.

text.p: More basis bids for hard red winter wheat were rolled out to the July contract, and grain dealers said Monday that farmer sales of wheat were extremely slow.
"I don't think producers know what to do. A lot of guys don't want to contract any new crop bushels because no one has a grasp on what they're going to raise," a north-central Oklahoma dealer said.
Meanwhile, one grain merchandising company in south-central Kansas was taking three cents per bushel protection on hard red winter wheat.
"Chicago traded about three cents lower overnight, so we're tacking on three cents just to be on the safe side," a dealer said.

Wheat growing areas of Texas and Oklahoma received rain Thursday through Saturday, but dealers said northwest Kansas and Nebraska missed out on the precipitation. Clear, open weather conditions were expected this week in the central and southern U.S. Plains.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: K=KCBT May wheat futures. N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
